title: Verdant 40 — Atlas: Parchment & Natural Colour World Map Tileset for RPG Maker MZ, Tiled & Godot [16x16]
shortText: A world map tileset drawn like a chart, in paper and natural colour: 700 tiles, 35 landmarks. RPG Maker MZ, Tiled, Godot

description:
A world map drawn like a chart, and the same map in natural colour. 700 tiles at 16x16: every tile exists twice, once on parchment and once in natural colour, drawn once so the two line up exactly. Commercial use permitted in unlimited projects, no attribution required; you may not resell the tiles themselves as an asset pack.

Two palettes, one drawing

The paper palette (15 colours) is an old printed chart: parchment land, a pale blue sea, sepia ink. The natural palette (36 colours) is the same map as a JRPG world: green land, blue water, grey peaks with snow caps, red roofs. There are 350 twin pairs, and the sheets come in twins laid out cell for cell, so in Tiled or Godot you can swap one sheet image for its twin and the whole map changes palette without moving a tile. The GIF above is exactly that swap, wiped across the map.

What is in it

  • 470 transition tiles in 10 complete 47-mask sets, five per palette: the coast (an ink shoreline with a line of water-lining offshore), the shallow shelf, and desert, snowfield and marsh regions. Every inner corner, outer corner, edge, junction and single is there.
  • 36 ground tiles per palette: deep ocean, shallow sea, land, forest, hills, mountain range, marsh, desert and snow, four variants each. Forests, hills and mountains are drawn as glyphs on land, the way a chart draws them, so they need no transition tiles.
  • 35 landmarks per palette: capital, city, town, village, hamlet, castle, fort, tower, wizard tower, ruins, temple, shrine, cave, mine, camp, port, lighthouse, windmill, farm, oasis, pyramid, volcano, standing stones, obelisk, a great tree, a dead wood, a graveyard, a skull, crossed swords, treasure, a flag, a ship, a sea serpent, a whirlpool and a portal. All transparent, so they lie over any ground.
  • 32 river and road pieces per palette: a meandering river and a dashed road for all 15 ways a tile can connect, plus a bridge each way; any two pieces join.
  • Chart furniture: an eight-point compass rose (3x3 tiles), a map border with four corners, and a title cartouche that stretches to any width, left blank for your own lettering.
  • A finished 40x26 sample map in both palettes, as PNG and JSON with every cell named by tile id; the paper map also as a Tiled .tmx. tiles.json gives every tile's role, palette, twin, sheet slot, mask and passability.

Engines

  • RPG Maker MZ: both palettes on one tileset, the paper sets in A2 slots 1 to 5 and the natural sets in 6 to 10, with every tile also on the B, C and D pages. Every A2 shape was composed back out of the sheet with MZ's own autotile table (480 of 480 identical). Tested against the table, not inside the MZ editor.
  • Tiled: one .tsx per sheet; Tiled's own renderer drew the paper sample map identical to ours (1,064,960 px, 0 differ).
  • Godot 4: one TileSet, loaded and verified in Godot 4.7.2 (700 tiles built).

Nothing in this pack animates.

The proofs

Every tile's wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4x4 repetition is rendered and reviewed. Grid, palette and autotile completeness are machine-proven: every tile is exactly 16x16, every pixel is inside the 47-colour palette, and alpha is strictly on or off. Every paper tile was checked against its natural twin: same size, same silhouette.

More from the series

Verdant 01 — Overworld is the same kind of world at walking scale, and Verdant Hex 01 is strategy terrain on a hex grid.

AI disclosure

Every tile is generated by our own procedural drawing engine, which is AI-written software. No image model, no scraped art and no training dataset were used, and nothing was traced.
